pages.text: A falling body follows a $(thing)geodesic$(): the straightest path through curved spacetime. The $(item)Geodesic Compass$() points along one. A mass squeezed inside $(thing)r_s = 2GM/c²$() lets no light out.
Light follows geodesics too, and is bent by $(thing)α = 4GM/(c²b)$() - 1.75″ at the Sun's edge. A mass exactly in front of a star turns it into an Einstein ring.

The $(item)Lensing Concentrator$() aims at a star through a lens mass and turns the focused light into power - at night, under open sky. The magnification $(thing)A = (u² + 2)/(u√(u² + 4))$() grows without limit as the alignment u → 0, but the aim jitters by 0.3 milliarcseconds: choose a massive, near lens so the Einstein radius is big. Above A = 20 it grows an $(item)Einstein Ring Lens$().
